features_used: realised growth of the country's trade with the rest of the world excluding Russia, Ukraine and Belarus, same direction, total (UN Comtrade, own report), nominal and deflated by the flow's price index
the same for non-fuel goods and for fuel (HS 27) separately; the 2021 fuel share of imports from Russia
realised trade by HS chapter with the world and Russia (60 largest partners; share models only)
realised real GDP growth and real imports/exports of goods and services volume growth (World Bank WDI)
realised commodity price changes in EUR: crude oil, European gas, Australian coal, base metals, fertilisers, grains, food, non-energy (World Bank Pink Sheet)
UN General Assembly ideal-point distance to Russia (Ukraine) at the last pre-origin year and its change over the previous 5 years (Bailey, Strezhnev and Voeten; pre-origin values only)

the flow's own momentum to the origin (1-year and 3-year average log growth), its share of rest-of-world trade, base size, horizon, flow type, EU and 2022-sanctioning-country flags, the change in the flow's price index
hub side (tested, not used for the counterfactual): Russia's or Ukraine's realised trade of the same type with non-sanctioning countries and with all other partners, and the hub's real GDP
notes: Nowcasting back-test: 16 models, three tests (origins 2008, 2013, 2016), median absolute log error 1-5 years ahead against the random walk. Realised predictors from the country's own side (its trade with the rest of the world, GDP, import volume) and commodity prices help in normal and boom years (2008, 2016 origins) but not when the shock comes from the Russian side (2013 origin: oil crash, rouble devaluation, 2014 counter-sanctions). Only Russia-side controls (Russia's trade with other partners) help in all three tests, and those are not usable for 2022-2026 because the war reshaped all of Russia's trade. Chosen: exports to Russia - pooled linear nowcast (gain 17.7%, all tests positive); Ukraine flows - linear nowcast (buy_ukr, 18.2%) and random forest (sell_ukr, 24.6%), two tests only and weaker evidence for large flows; imports from Russia and services - random walk (2021 level; services with the travel gap closing at the UNWTO pace). For 2022-2026 the commodity-price features use the IMF WEO October 2021 (pre-war) path, not realised war-affected prices; central values are midway between using the country's trade excluding Russia/Ukraine/Belarus and its total trade (sourcing switches); re-export hubs and Belarus are held at the 2021 level. Intervals: 5th-95th percentiles of the chosen model's back-test errors by flow and size class, scaled by horizon (about h^0.5).

models.rw: random walk: last pre-origin year (2021 for the counterfactual) held flat in real terms
models.sh_last: the flow's share of the country's trade with the rest of the world (excluding Russia, Ukraine, Belarus; same direction) held at the last pre-origin level; realised rest-of-world trade
models.sh_avg: the same share held at its 4-year pre-origin average
models.sh_fuel: share held separately for fuel (HS 27) and non-fuel trade (imports from Russia); non-fuel rest-of-world trade for the other goods flows
models.sh_hs: share held by HS chapter (Russia's 24 largest export chapters for imports from Russia, 24 largest import chapters for exports to Russia, plus a rest-of-trade chapter; 60 largest partners), summed
models.elastic: pooled elasticity of the flow to real rest-of-world trade, fitted on pre-origin years
models.gdp: the country's realised real GDP growth applied to the last level (unit elasticity)
models.vol: the country's realised real import (or export) volume of goods and services applied to the last level
models.hub_donor: Russia's (Ukraine's) realised trade of the same type with countries that did not sanction Russia in 2022 (excluding the country itself); hub-side control
models.hub_all: Russia's (Ukraine's) realised trade of the same type with all other partners; hub-side control
models.elastic_hub: pooled elasticities to rest-of-world trade and to the hub-side donor-pool trade
models.lin: pooled robust linear nowcast (Huber) on the features below, fitted on pre-origin year pairs
models.rf: random forest on the same features, fitted on pre-origin year pairs
models.gbm: gradient-boosted trees (absolute-error loss) on the same features, fitted on pre-origin year pairs
models.gbm_hub: gradient-boosted trees with hub-side features added (Russia's/Ukraine's trade with other partners, hub GDP)
models.gbm_xo: gradient-boosted trees fitted on all year pairs outside the test window (also later years); diagnostic only, not eligible

tests.T2008: origin 2008: data to 2007, predicting 2008-2012 (1-5 years ahead)
tests.T2013: origin 2013: data to 2012, predicting 2013, 2016, 2017 (2014-2015 Crimea/Donbas excluded); Ukraine flows excluded (post-2014 Ukrainian trade is a war outcome)
tests.T2016: origin 2016: data to 2016, predicting 2017-2019 and 2021 (2020 COVID excluded; services also without 2021)

decision_rule: per flow type, the eligible model with the lowest mean (over tests) median absolute log error, 1-5 years ahead, is used if it beats the random walk by at least 15% in every test, or by at least 15% on average with no test worse; otherwise the random walk. Hub-side models are not eligible (their 2022-2026 inputs were reshaped by the war), nor is gbm_xo (trained on later years).
units: level_2021: EUR bn, nominal (low/high = range of own and partner reports). multiplier_vs_2021: real (volume at 2018-2021 prices), relative to the 2021 level. eur_bn_at_2018_2021_prices: 2021 level revalued at the 2018-2021 average price of the flow x multiplier. 2026 = January-August, expressed as an annual rate.
